_comment: load_bearing_no_subject is the count of claims that assert a SECURITY control and name
nothing a machine can resolve: no code-quoted symbol, no path, no env var. It is where two
of the eleven original defects lived - the compose comment attributing rate limiting to
redis while nothing constructed RedisCounter, and the fourteen docstrings saying a
credential was never logged without naming what made that so.
This number MAY ONLY DECREASE. That is the goal document's own and only success criterion,
and until this file existed nothing measured it.
Lowering it means giving a claim a resolvable subject, not deleting the claim. Deleting a
true claim to make a number fall would be the worst possible use of this file, and the
reason the summary prints the ORDINARY residue beside it is so that rewording a claim to
dodge the phrase list is visible as a rise on the other side of the ledger.
note: 236 at the first census, 231 after the first decrement, 226 after the next structural pass, 217 after the 2026-07-29 Worker-primary extraction pass, 216 after the Worker-primary capability-honesty pass, 215 after the full new-source inventory made another control claim name its mechanism, and 208 after the primary-surface/native-recovery pass made seven more load-bearing claims name their implementation subjects. The auth surface's nine keys-only claims rested on nothing but the care of whoever wrote each line; five now name the mechanism they rest on (`_audit`, and the fact that the material is ABSENT from the dict rather than filtered out of it) and all of them are proven by SEC-191, which drives login, failed login and 2FA enrolment and searches the whole audit stream for the password, the session secret, the CSRF token and the otpauth URI. Shown to fail: seeding the login row with the password and the csrf reddens two of the three cases. The third neuters pii.contains_secret and requires no change, so the guarantee cannot quietly become the scrubber's. The first CI run of this gate went red where local was green: the census was walking the filesystem and read docker-compose.override.yml, which is gitignored local development config, so it contributed two rows here and none in CI. The source set is now bounded by `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`: ignored local configuration remains invisible, while a non-ignored new module is counted before staging. A gate measuring environment-dependent claims that was itself environment-dependent is the Tier 3 family arriving inside the tool built to measure it, and it was caught by the byte-identical regeneration check rather than by anyone noticing. 206 after the origin/main merge. The merge was the interesting case for this ratchet: the decision-0021 tree had driven the residue to 208 while fourteen commits landed on origin/main independently, and merging them raised it to 210 - four new load-bearing claims naming nothing, two old ones gone. A ratchet that only ever sees one lineage would have called that a pass, because neither side regressed against its own baseline; the growth existed only in the union. The four were all the same shape and none was unfounded prose: each claim's mechanism was code-quoted on the PREVIOUS line, because the sentence wrapped. The census reads a line at a time, so a symbol one line above the claim is a symbol the census cannot see. Rewrapped so each claim and its subject sit together (``SecurityWriter`` in api/host_boundary.py and kernel/hitl_http.py, ``APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS_FLOOR`` in config/manifest.py, ``audit_detail`` in kernel/schema_diagnosis.py) - which is a readability improvement as much as a census one, and cost the first attempt two rounds because moving the symbol to the line ABOVE the claim phrase changes nothing.
